text:
Mackenzie Blackwood has the record of a goalie on a contender, 11-3-1 through 16 starts, and the underlying numbers of a goalie doing his job without stealing much. In Colorado, that's not a complaint.

He has saved 2.4 goals more than the shots he faced usually allow (goals saved above expected), 64th percentile, on a .905 save percentage. Our wins-added measure has him squarely mid-pack, 38th of 77 goalies. Where he earns his keep is on the hard looks: .742 on high-danger shots against a league .685. On low-danger shots, the ones goalies are supposed to eat, he's right at league average.

The month has had a dip and a response. Columbus chased him after 32 minutes on Nov. 3; four nights later he shut out Detroit. Toronto scored three on him on Nov. 10, and he answered by allowing one goal to Montreal on Nov. 14.

Last season he was part of a Jennings Trophy win and saved 8.0 goals above expected in 39 games, so the steady version is the one we've seen before. He gets Utah tonight, with Sebastian Cossa in the other net.
